title: Derivative expansion in algebraic normal form
statement: Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $f\colon\mathbb{F}_2^n\to\mathbb{F}_2$, and let $y\in\mathbb{F}_2^n$. For each subset $S$ of the coordinates, define $a_S=\displaystyle\sum_{T\subseteq S} f(1_T)$ in $\mathbb{F}_2$, where $1_T$ is the vector whose coordinates in $T$ are $1$ and whose other coordinates are $0$. Then, for every $x\in\mathbb{F}_2^n$, $f(x)+f(x+y)=\displaystyle\sum_{S\subseteq\{0,\ldots,n-1\}}a_S\bigl(m_S(x)+m_S(x+y)\bigr)$, where $m_S(z)=\prod_{i\in S}z_i$.
hypotheses_covered: A function f from the n-dimensional Boolean cube to F₂
A direction y in the n-dimensional Boolean cube
